thesis: UPDATE TO EXISTING POSITION - HOLD, do not add. Opened 2026-09-11 at 49.60, now 50.23 (+1.3%), one session old. Today research strengthens rather than changes the thesis: the inflation the Fed is hiking against on Wednesday is itself an energy supply shock, with WTI at $99.99 and roughly 10M bbl/day cut from global output at the peak of the Hormuz disruption. Devon sits above a rising SMA20 48.27, SMA50 45.45 and SMA200 43.79, within 4.7% of its 400-day high.
key_risk: The stop is 46.90 and the entire position rests on one geopolitical fact. A credible Hormuz re-opening or ceasefire gaps every name in this lane through its stop at once - and this report now holds three correlated energy exposures (DVN, XLE, DINO), which is the cap from config/strategy.md and means the lane cannot be diversified further.
counter_argument: Six months after the shock, supply re-routing is the base case rather than the tail, and the ECB has already published that oil and gas prices rose less than expected. Buying oil beta at $100 crude, three days before a Fed hike explicitly designed to destroy demand, is late.

evidence.detail: Close 50.23 on 2026-09-11, above a rising SMA20 48.2675, SMA50 45.451 and SMA200 43.7888, with a 400-day range of 25.89-52.71 (-4.7% off the high). ATR14 1.177; the 46.90 stop is 2.29 ATR from the 49.60 entry, clearing the 2.0 stock floor.

Sector leadership is measured, not assumed: XLE returned +6.73% over 1m and +14.04% over 3m against SPY at -1.06% and +3.60% - the only sector on today board within 2% of its 400-day high while bond proxies sit at 150-day lows.

catalyst.event: FOMC decision Wed 2026-09-16 14:00 ET with a 25bp hike at 79c and a further hike priced for December at 59c; the 2-year at 4.56% already sits ~93bp above effective fed funds at 3.63%
catalyst.action: UPDATE TO AN EXISTING POSITION - REAFFIRM the exit/avoid published 2026-09-02 at 81.87. Stay out of long duration through Wednesday. This is an avoid, not a short - do not initiate a leveraged bearish bond position at a 150-day low

thesis: UPDATE TO EXISTING POSITION - REAFFIRM. The avoid-duration call published 2026-09-02 at 81.87 is working, TLT now 80.87 (+1.2%), and the reason has strengthened rather than decayed. The front end is already pricing tightening - the 2-year at 4.56% sits about 93bp ABOVE effective fed funds at 3.63% - and the market prices a 79% chance the Fed validates that on Wednesday plus another hike in December. A prior TLT LONG in this book was stopped out on 2026-09-10, which is the same fact learned the expensive way.
key_risk: TLT is at 80.87 against a 150-day low of 80.665 - it is 0.25% off the low, which is exactly where a violent short-covering rally starts if the statement reads as one-and-done. The honest risk of this call is opportunity cost rather than loss, since it is an avoid rather than a position; but reaffirming a bearish duration view at the low is the mirror image of the mistake that stopped out the TLT long.
counter_argument: A credible hawkish hike can pull long-end inflation expectations DOWN and rally the 20-year even as the front end sells off - that is what a Fed getting ahead of a supply shock is supposed to do. The Chicago Fed models the shock as cutting 2026 growth by 81-166bp, and a growth scare is the classic bid for duration. TLT at a 150-day low with a hike fully priced is not an obvious place to stay bearish.

evidence.detail: FOMC 2026-09-16 read from the Kalshi contract rules; hike-25 last 79c vs hold 21c, and December hike-25 at 59c. The path, not just the meeting, is priced hawkish.
TLT closed 80.87 on 2026-09-11, 0.25% above its 150-day low of 80.665 and 11.0% below the 150-day high of 90.86, beneath SMA20 82.20 and SMA50 82.9878. ATR14 0.659 (0.82%).

The curve itself is the position read: US 2-year 4.56% and 10-year 4.95% (both 2026-09-10) against effective fed funds of 3.63% (2026-09-10), with the 10y-2y spread at +33bp on 2026-09-11. A front end 93bp above the policy rate is the bond market pricing hikes, not cuts, and PPI accelerating to 5.4% annual in August is what moved it there.

catalyst.action: WAIT for a close above the 295.28 SMA200, then buy 295.50-302.00. Do NOT buy at the current 284.75 - the level that defines this idea has not been taken yet

thesis: Constellation is the cleanest listed claim on nuclear baseload sold to datacenters, and it has been de-rated 31% from its 400-day high as a long-duration growth asset while the 10-year went to 4.95%. The tape is now turning underneath that: CEG has reclaimed SMA20 281.54 and SMA50 269.53 and sits 3.7% under its SMA200, while outperforming XLU by 11.82 points over three months and 3.24 over one - the sector it is benchmarked against is at 150-day lows and CEG is not following it down.
key_risk: Sell-side positioning is crowded and has not capitulated: 82.1% bullish, 5 strong buy and 18 buy against 5 holds and zero sells, on a stock down 31%. That leaves downgrade risk entirely ahead rather than behind, and CEG carries a 3.25% ATR so a de-rating leg moves fast. The idea also has no dated catalyst - it is a trend-change bet, which is the weakest kind of thesis in this report.
counter_argument: Every rate-sensitive long-duration asset on today board is below its 200-day for the same reason, and a Fed hiking on Wednesday with a further hike priced for December makes that worse, not better. Calling a bottom in the most rate-sensitive growth complex three days before a hike is fighting the one force that has actually been driving prices all year.

catalyst.event: Nymex 3:2:1 crack spread near $69.92/bbl against a $21.68 ten-year average, plus a planned separation of the Lubricants & Specialties segment into an independent public company over the next 12-18 months
catalyst.action: buy at market on the next open (Mon 2026-09-14) inside 105.50-109.50; add only above the 112.165 400-day high

thesis: HF Sinclair earns the crack spread rather than the crude price, and that spread is at an extreme: the Nymex 3:2:1 sits near $69.92/bbl against a $21.68 average for the decade to Feb 2026. The 8-K shows it converting - Q2 2026 adjusted refinery gross margin of $25.95 per produced barrel sold versus $16.50 a year earlier, and net income of $892 million or $4.93 per diluted share against $208 million or $1.10. Separately and independently of the spread, management is separating the Lubricants & Specialties segment into a listed company over 12-18 months, which is a structural value-unlock that does not depend on crude staying where it is.
key_risk: This is peak-cycle earnings and the multiple lies about it. $4.93 of quarterly EPS annualises to roughly 5.5x at 107.84, which looks cheap and is the classic refiner value trap - a low P/E on a cyclical top is a warning, not a bargain, because the denominator is about to fall. Crack spreads are the most violently mean-reverting number in energy and this one is three times its ten-year average purely because Hormuz transit is impaired; a ceasefire re-rates DINO down 30% in days through any sane stop.
counter_argument: CNBC ran the bear case explicitly on 2026-08-17: refiner stocks are on a nearly unprecedented run and history says it ends soon. DINO is +88% over six months and +22.6% in the last month, and the last three refining cycles all ended with the spread collapsing faster than the equity did.

evidence.detail: Read the Q2 2026 8-K. Exact figures: adjusted refinery gross margin $25.95 per produced barrel sold vs $16.50 in Q2 2025 (+57%); net income attributable to stockholders $892 million, or $4.93 per diluted share, vs $208 million or $1.10 a year earlier (+329%). The company plans to separate its Lubricants & Specialties segment through the capital markets into an independent, publicly traded company over the next 12-18 months, and will retire its Mississauga, Ontario base oil refining assets by 2027 while keeping regional blending via new sourcing agreements.

Open-market insider buying: 3 purchases by 2 distinct buyers totalling $2.42M over six months, net +$705K against sales. Franklin Myers bought 15,000 shares at $69.11 on 2026-05-18 and another 15,000 at $85.30 on 2026-08-11 - a repeat purchase after the run was well advanced. Relative strength: DINO +22.64% 1m vs XLE +6.73% and SPY -1.06%; +88.24% 6m vs XLE +13.27%.

112.165 is the 400-day high, printed intraday on 2026-09-11 before closing 107.84, so it is a tested level rather than a round number. Support shelf 103.12-104.81 from the Sept 2-4 lows sits above a rising SMA20 at 100.294; SMA50 91.285 and SMA200 66.721 are far beneath. ATR14 3.897, so the 99.00 stop is 2.18 ATR from entry. Avg dollar volume $273M/day.

Against the CNBC mean-reversion case: the insider closest to the margin book bought again at 85.30 in August, after the run, rather than trimming; and the sell side is not crowded - analyst bullish share is only 52.2% (4 strong buy, 8 buy, 9 hold, 1 sell, 1 strong sell) and has FALLEN 2.3 points over four months. The Lubricants separation also gives a value path that survives a spread normalisation, which the pure mean-reversion case does not account for.
